name: Isosorbide mononitrate
route_note: extended-release tablet once daily or immediate-release twice daily with an eccentric (7-hour) interval
originator: Multiple companies (developed as the active metabolite of isosorbide dinitrate)

discovery.note: Identified as the main active metabolite of isosorbide dinitrate and developed as a drug that avoids first-pass metabolism.

tagline: Long-acting oral nitrate for preventing angina, dosed to avoid tolerance
summary: Isosorbide mononitrate is the active metabolite of isosorbide dinitrate, given orally to prevent angina. Unlike most nitrates it is not subject to first-pass metabolism, giving nearly complete bioavailability, and it is dosed with a nitrate-free interval to prevent tolerance.
mechanism: Organic nitrates are bioactivated in vascular smooth muscle to release nitric oxide. NO activates soluble guanylate cyclase, raising cyclic GMP, which lowers intracellular calcium and relaxes smooth muscle.

At usual doses veins dilate more than arteries, so venous return (preload) and myocardial oxygen demand fall; larger arteries, including coronary arteries and collaterals, also dilate. Continuous exposure causes tolerance, so a daily nitrate-free interval is used.
uses: Prevention of angina pectoris due to coronary artery disease

history.title: Nitrates enter angina treatment
history.detail: William Murrell reports in The Lancet that small doses of nitroglycerin relieve angina, founding the organic-nitrate drug class.

history.title: Mechanism uncovered
history.detail: Ferid Murad shows that nitroglycerin and related nitrates act by releasing nitric oxide, which activates soluble guanylyl cyclase in smooth muscle.

history.title: ISIS-4
history.detail: In a mega-trial of acute myocardial infarction, oral isosorbide mononitrate does not reduce 5-week mortality.

history.title: Nobel Prize for nitric oxide
history.detail: Furchgott, Ignarro and Murad are honoured for discovering nitric oxide signalling, the pathway through which nitrates act.

history.title: PDE5 interaction
history.detail: Sildenafil is approved with a contraindication for concomitant nitrate use.

history.title: NEAT-HFpEF
history.detail: Isosorbide mononitrate reduces daily activity levels and does not improve quality of life in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.

pk.metabolism: Hepatic denitration and glucuronidation; no first-pass

facts: It is not suitable for relief of an acute angina attack because of its slow onset.
Extended-release tablets should not be crushed or chewed.

references.title: Redfield MM et al. Isosorbide mononitrate in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (NEAT-HFpEF). N Engl J Med 2015
